scenario_name: LangGraph-style Approval Routing Graph — Case 4 for AgentCoordKG
description: Hand-authored scenario following LangGraph's real StateGraph/Node/Edge schema (confirmed via official LangGraph documentation), NOT a live LangGraph run. Demonstrates AgentCoordKG's coverage of a generic graph-execution framework, including the same disclosed Node-to-Agent interpretive judgment used in HarnessKG's LangGraph scenario, and a third independent confirmation that orchestration primitives (here, Edge) map onto AgentCoordKG's dependsOn rather than HarnessKG's vocabulary.

_langgraph_native_log._comment: Mimics a real LangGraph StateGraph definition for a two-step approval routing flow. Not itself part of the RDF instance data.

nodes.name: assess_node
nodes.description: Wraps an LLM call to assess a request for risk -- mapped to ak:Agent

nodes.name: route_check_node
nodes.description: Pure routing-logic function, no LLM call -- NOT mapped to ak:Agent

nodes.name: escalate_node
nodes.description: Wraps an LLM call to handle escalated/flagged requests -- mapped to ak:Agent

_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Node (function processing State) -- INTE: Same disclosed rule as HarnessKG's LangGraph scenario: a Node is mapped to ak:Agent ONLY when it wraps an LLM call (assess_node, escalate_node here); route_check_node (pure logic, no LLM call) is NOT mapped to ak:Agent. This is our design choice, not a LangGraph-enforced distinction.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Edge (connects Nodes, sequential or cond: THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: maps directly to dependsOn (Task -> Task), when each Node's unit of work is modeled as a Task. This is the third framework (after CrewAI's Process and AutoGen's GroupChatManager) whose native orchestration primitive lands cleanly on AgentCoordKG's dependsOn relation rather than requiring any HarnessKG vocabulary.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.State (TypedDict shared data): NO AgentCoordKG equivalent -- State is HarnessKG's territory (maps to hk:Memory there). This is the second independent confirmation (after CrewAI's Crew-level memory=True) that a framework's memory-flavored primitive has no home in AgentCoordKG, while its orchestration-flavored primitives (Edge here) do -- reinforcing the same clean division of labor.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Checkpointer (cross-session State persis: NO AgentCoordKG equivalent, same reasoning as State above -- belongs to HarnessKG.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.Conditional Edge routing outcome (risk_f: Interpreted (not native to LangGraph) as triggering ak:Decision -- same treatment as HarnessKG's LangGraph scenario and consistent with the task-outcome Decisions found in AgentCoordKG's other framework scenarios.
_mapping_decision_tree_notes.risk_flag=True condition (assessment ide: Interpreted (not native to LangGraph) as violatesConstraint -> Conflict, consistent with the interpretive pattern used across all AgentCoordKG framework scenarios so far.

story_summary: A LangGraph node assesses an incoming request and flags it as too risky, creating a conflict. The flagged request is then routed to an escalation node, which handles it and produces the routing decision.
